correctness.rationale: Sylvester symmetry gives c/2 elements of the semigroup below c when zero is included; replacing zero by the absorber leaves that size unchanged. The minimal positive summand is a, so the first length at which all words vanish is ceil(c/a); when a=c=2 the quotient is just the absorber and the formula is still correct. For the reconstruction, c >= a(a-1), and if h=ceil(c/a), then c/a <= h < c/a+1 <= c/(a-1), whence a=ceil(c/h) and b=1+c/(a-1). This independently verifies the frozen strict reconstruction. For a=2, b is absent and any nontrivial quotient is monogenic. For a>=3 both generators are present and are precisely the indecomposables; the powers of b first vanish at a-1, whereas the powers of a first vanish at length >=a if b>=a+2. Thus no exchange is then possible. For b=a+1 all nonempty monomials through degree a-2 survive, those of degree >=a-1 vanish, and the small monomials are distinct because a relation between a and a+1 needs exponent changes divisible by a+1 and a, respectively. Exchange is therefore an actual order-two automorphism, not just a candidate permutation. Inspected the frozen finite checker and recorded output without executing the checker; the uniform proof does not depend on either.

value.rationale: A natural unbounded class of quotients from the symmetric-semigroup rigidity conjecture is completely classified by two inexpensive intrinsic invariants, and the exact nonrigid automorphism family is identified.
